observations.body: Timothy joins and is circumcised. He came to Derbe and Lystra; and behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timothy, the son of a Jewess who believed, but his father was a Greek. So the assemblies were strengthened in the faith, and increased in number daily.
observations.label: Timothy joins and is circumcised

payload.posture: Read Acts 16:1–5 as one movement in Paul's story, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states timothy joins and is circumcised. He came to Derbe and Lystra; and behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timothy, the son of a Jewess who believed, but his father was a Greek. So the assemblies were strengthened in the faith, and increased in number daily. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of Paul's story.
